question: Players that stop dribbling in handball have to pass or shot within :
solution:
The correct answer is __**3 second.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ​A player commits a **"walking" offence** if they take more than** three steps **without **dribbling, passing, or shooting the ball.**
 
• Additionally, if the player has the ball for more than** three seconds,** this may occur.
 
• This guideline is sometimes referred to as the** "three-step rule."**
 
• A player that is **dribbling has three steps **to halt before they are **penalized for walking, which causes a turnover.**
 
• After that, each player has **three seconds to pass or shot.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In the team **sport of handball, two teams of seven players **each pass a ball with their hands in an effort to toss it towards the** opposite team's goal.**
 
• **Two 30-minute quarters **make up a typical game, and the team with the **most goals wins.**
 
• A goal is located in the **centre of each end of the 40 by the 20-meter court** on which modern handball is played.
